_comment: Style catalogue for render_map.py. A layer's `style` may name one of these categories. Shape and pattern are the identity of a category; colours are references resolved from theme.json (`auto`, `auto:<family>`, `fixed:<key>`, `risk:<level>`, `transparent`) or literal hex values. Keys starting with `_` are documentation and are ignored. Optional fields: `exclusion_type` (hard / review / soft) groups restriction layers in the legend and in drawing order; `categorize_by` + `categories` and `rules` build categorized or rule-based renderers from a single table; `casing_color` / `casing_width_mm` draw a halo under a line; `legend_*` fields override only the legend swatch. Rasters are not styled here; they take min/max/colors in the layer config.

land_use._note: Bare `auto` takes the next colour of the global qualitative counter in config order and does not know semantics: the same real-world entity split across several layer keys may get different colours. When colours must match across layers or maps, use a `fixed:` colour instead.

contour._note: Same caveat as land_use: bare `auto` is order-based, not semantic.

restriction_forest._note: Protected forest treated as a hard exclusion by default: opaque solid fill so it reads differently from hatched soft buffers. Whether a given protected class is a legal exclusion must be confirmed for each jurisdiction; override with style_overrides: {exclusion_type: soft} where it is not. Related classes use protection_1..4 from the same green ramp so several protected classes on one map stay distinguishable.

restriction_protected_3._note: Third protected-land class (fixed:protection_3). Whether a class is a hard exclusion depends on the applicable rules; override exclusion_type where appropriate.

restriction_heritage._note: Cultural heritage protection treated as a hard exclusion by default. Where heritage rules only limit height or require consent, override exclusion_type to review or soft. Uses fixed:heritage (dark plum) so it is not mistaken for the warm turbine colours.

restriction_mining._note: Mining rights are usually a tenure or negotiation issue rather than a statutory exclusion, so they default to soft. Opacity is lower (0.3) than other soft buffers so large mining polygons do not dominate the figure.

restriction_aerodrome._note: Absolute aviation exclusion only. Red plus a cross hatch drawn over a translucent base fill (`hatch_over_fill`): the base makes a large area read as one block, the cross hatch keeps a non-colour cue that separates it from other red/orange categories. Aviation constraints that require a permit or aeronautical study (obstacle limitation surfaces, safeguarding zones) are not absolute exclusions; use restriction_review for those.

restriction_review._note: Restricted area that needs specific approval but is not an absolute exclusion (exclusion_type: review), for example aviation safeguarding surfaces. Keeps the high-risk red but uses a single hatch and lower opacity so it is visually weaker than hard exclusions. Which constraints belong here is a legal question for each jurisdiction, not a cartographic one.

restriction_review_secondary._note: Second variant of restriction_review with lower opacity (0.35), so two adjacent review layers on the same map can be told apart. Same meaning; the legend lists them separately.

road_paved._note: Road lines use a casing (a pale halo drawn under the line) so they stay visible on any basemap instead of relying on a colour that happens to contrast with one particular basemap. `legend_casing_color` applies only to the legend swatch, whose near-white background needs a darker casing than the map. Layer opacity 0.7 and a narrow casing keep dense road networks in the background.

building_predicted._note: Outline only: the same filled = confirmed / hollow = predicted convention as building_confirmed.

other_project_point._note: Point features of third-party projects. Circle instead of the triangle of other_project, so two kinds of third-party point in the same map are separated by shape while sharing the reference colour family.

priority_zone._note: Generic land-attribute or zoning polygon. Opacity 0.65 so the lighter qualitative colours remain visible over a muted basemap. Bare `auto` is order-based: if several zoning layers must keep consistent colours across maps, give each a fixed colour (for example via style_overrides: {color: ...}).

restriction_military._note: Military zones treated as a hard exclusion by default; confirm locally.

restriction_flood._note: Flood-prone areas: a probabilistic risk rather than a statutory exclusion, so soft. Blue from the grid family to suggest water while staying distinct from permanent water bodies (fixed:water).

other_project_boundary._note: Boundary of a third-party project: outline only, reference colour family, so it is not confused with restriction fills.

alert_point._note: Individual features that need attention (for example a turbine with a confirmed conflict): a red star that cannot be confused with the regular turbine symbol.

turbine_position_phase._note: Ring-set turbine symbol with the outer ring coloured by a group field (`categorize_by`). The example categories expect values 1/2/3 in a field named `phase`; replace them per project with style_overrides, e.g. {categorize_by: stage, categories: {A: {label: ..., ring_outer_color: fixed:group_1}}}. `color: transparent` is set explicitly because point_ringset does not use it and a default `auto` would consume a colour from the global counter.

turbine_position_ringset._note: Ring-set turbine symbol (outer ring, inner ring, centre dot) without grouping. The outer ring is a literal colour rather than auto:own_infra so the same turbine layer keeps the same colour when it is reused by several layer keys; an auto:family reference would advance the family counter each time.

boundary_by_phase._note: Group boundary with dashed outline and light fill, coloured like the matching turbine_position_phase outer ring so readers can pair a boundary with its turbines without the legend. The example categories expect values 1/2/3 in a field named `phase`; replace them per project.

boundary_overall._note: Overall site boundary: heavy dark outline, no fill, distinct from dashed group boundaries.

developable_area._note: Output of derive_developable_area.py: site minus the union of true exclusion layers, drawn as a single flat fill (risk:none). Only subtract layers that are real exclusions; layers that merely require review should be overlaid with restriction_review instead of being subtracted. If the derivation used a particular convention (for example setbacks measured from building footprints), state it in the figure caption.

exclusion_overlap._note: The `exclusion_union` layer of derive_developable_area.py, classed by how many constraints overlap at each place (a count-based simplification of the constraint-overlap analysis in Ryberg, Robinius & Stolten 2018, land eligibility in Europe). Colours are ColorBrewer 'Purples' (6 classes), a single-hue sequential scheme suited to counts and chosen to stay clear of the orange turbine colours.

noise_contour._note: Generic noise contour lines (fields such as level_db). Lines only, no fill, with the value labelled on the line: set label_field: "level_db || ' dB'" and label_placement: curved in the layer config. Pick the criterion contour out of the same table with a `filter` and style it with noise_contour_limit.

noise_contour_limit._note: The contour that corresponds to the applicable criterion, selected from the noise_contour table with a `filter`. Coloured fixed:status_exceed.

flicker_isoline._note: Shadow-flicker isolines: uniform dark grey thin lines; the classes themselves are carried by flicker_band fills. The key threshold line uses flicker_isoline_key.

flicker_isoline_key._note: The key shadow-flicker threshold line of the applicable guidance (for example 30 h/year in the German LAI shadow-flicker guidance, 2020 update): heavy black line that stays visible over any band colour. The threshold is chosen with a `filter` in the layer config.

receptor._note: Noise / flicker receptors: white square with dark outline, distinguished from turbines (circles) by shape. Pair with label_field for receptor IDs; use receptor_exceed with a filter such as exceeds = 1 for receptors above a criterion.

receptor_exceed._note: Receptor above the criterion: red square (fixed:status_exceed) with white outline.

flicker_band._note: Shadow-flicker hour bands as filled polygons (field hours_min). Multi-hue classes instead of lightness steps of one hue, by analogy with NatureScot (2017) para. 60, which advises against single-hue lightness steps for ZTV visibility bands. Colours are matplotlib 'plasma' sampled at 0.92 / 0.62 / 0.30: perceptually ordered and well separated in lightness, so classes remain readable in greyscale. Class limits are an example; override `rules` for the guidance in use. Draw one flicker case (e.g. astronomical maximum) per map. Band labels follow the data: when no level above 30 h/year is computed, the top band reads "30 h/year and above" rather than a fixed 30–100 range.

point_generic._note: Fallback for point layers without a `style`.

line_generic._note: Fallback for line layers without a `style`.

polygon_generic._note: Fallback for polygon layers without a `style`.
